title: The Ability of Three Different Protocols in Removing Biroceramic- and Resin based Sealers from Simulated Internal Root Resorption Cavities: An in vitro Study
protocol: Remove crowns using a sterile diamond disk to standardize root length to 18 mm.
Prepare an access cavity using sterile diamond burs.
Extirpate pulp using #10 K-files.
Determine working length with a #15 K-file, 1mm short of where the file is visible from the apical foramen.
Mechanically prepare the root canal to size #35:0.06.
Irrigate the prepared canal with NaOCl 5.25% using a 27-gauge needle, 1mm short of working length.
Final irrigation with 5 mL distilled water.
Dry the canal with paper points.
Prepare simulated internal root canal resorption according to Topçuoğlu et al.
Fix specimens in modified silicon (hydrorise, Zhermack, Italy) within an eppendorf tube.
After silicone setting, remove the specimen from the eppendorf tube.
Create two longitudinal grooves along the root on both buccal and lingual sides using sterile diamond burs.
Split the specimen along its long axis with a chisel.
Make standard cavities on both segments 5 mm from the apex.
Cavities should be 0.8 mm deep and 1.6 mm in diameter.
Use sterile diamond burs under water cooling for cavity preparation.
Keep 7 random specimens as a negative control group with no further treatment.
Fill the cavities of 36 random specimens with resin-based sealer and assign to group A.
Fill the cavities of another 36 random specimens with bioceramic sealer and assign to group B.
Bond back together the two halves of each specimen using superglue and remount in silicon impression for proper positioning.
Seal the access cavity with a temporary filling.
Store all specimens at 37°C at 100% humidity for 1 week.
Split each specimen again after storing under specified conditions for evaluation.
Capture one digital image of each half of the split specimens under an inverted laboratory microscope (Leica DM IL LED).
Evaluate images using the classification described by Van der Sluis et al.
Score 0: the cavity is free of debris.
Score 1: less than half of the cavity is filled with debris.
Score 2: more than half of the cavity is filled.
Score 3: the cavity is filled completely.
